newsitem.title: UK: Northwest to up ex-UK cargo rates 2-5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Northwest to up ex-UK cargo rates 2-5 pct.

text.p: Northwest Airlines Inc plans to increase its ex-UK cargo rates to the United States by between two and five percent from April 1, said its Atlantic division cargo manager Brian Mutton.
He said a two percent rise would be implemented on the carrier's London-Houston route, with five percent increases introduced to the U.S. west coast and destinations including Portland.
"Apart from fuel surcharges, these are our first ex-UK cargo rate increases since March 1995. They are going up because our costs continue to spiral," Mutton told Reuters.
"Airlines cannot afford to sustain losses any more. We are not a charity," he said.
He added that fuel surcharges were a separate issue to cargo rate rises.

"From September 1995 to September 1996, Northwest's fuel costs went up 28 percent and during that period we absorbed them. Apart from their suddenness, the fuel surcharge we did eventually impose received no basic complaints from the air cargo industry," he said.
